1.explanation:
1. src/menu/view/item.jsx: This file contains the logic for rendering individual menu items, including the current implementation of setting the 'title' attribute. The bug report and images directly reference this behavior, and any change to when/how the title is set must be made here.
2. src/menu/view/menu.jsx: This is the main Menu component, which manages the rendering and behavior of menu items. If the logic for passing down or controlling the 'title' attribute is to be centralized or made configurable, changes may be needed here.
3. src/select/base.jsx: The Select component uses menu items for its dropdown options. The images show the Select dropdown with tooltips, so changes to how titles are set for Select options may require updates here, especially if Select wraps or customizes menu item rendering.
4. src/cascader/item.jsx: The Cascader component also uses menu items, and the bug report mentions Cascader and CascaderSelect. If the title logic is to be consistent across all menu-like components, this file may need to be updated to match the new behavior for when to set the title attribute.
1.bug_scenario: The bug scenario concerns the use of the HTML 'title' attribute on menu items (such as dropdowns, select options, and cascader menus). Currently, the title is always set to the menu item's text, which causes a tooltip to appear on hover and is read by screen readers. This is helpful for accessibility and for showing truncated text, but it violates WCAG guidelines when the title is identical to the visible text (causing redundant information for screen readers) and is unwanted by some users. The images show tooltips appearing on menu items, both when the text is truncated (ellipsis) and when it is not, illustrating the redundancy and potential annoyance. The bug report discusses possible solutions, such as only setting the title when the text is truncated or when the menu item is a pure string, and not setting it for custom content.
